kind: Original public execution receipts; this documentation review did not reacquire their private raw archives

receipts.body:
Server CPU verification completed on 2026-11-11 for exact head `b1d965fea7f84b19cb9f61974bdb263de8d854c3` (tree `a7323b49512567eb26b5ab68294737280643be37`): **64 passed, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped**. This is the requested final 55-test set plus 8 request-organization regressions and the existing v1 event-sink integration case, not a sum with earlier runs.

Both optional prerequisites were actually exercised: installed LOTUS image preparation on generated CPU image fixtures (`SEMLOOM_REAL_LOTUS_MEDIA_CPU=1`), and the original vLLM 0.25.1 v1 graph-choice function extracted from the fixed 341,416-byte source (SHA-256 `6c92ded8468f44d6df863a617ce588f132fa6df7031feecc0cc421702a41610e`). The latter tests CPU branches with a fixture dispatcher; it does not construct the native engine. Software decision events also passed through the actual JSONL sink and execute-identity association.

Actual server environment: Python 3.12.3, LOTUS 1.2.4, Pillow **12.2.0**, Transformers 4.57.6, tokenizers 0.22.2, Ray 2.56.1 and PyArrow 24.0.0. Pillow differs from the earlier local 13.0.0 environment; no packages were changed. CPU 0–7 was enforced and read back, INET/INET6 were blocked before SDK imports and in Python fixture children. No model, Ray runtime or GPU work ran; CUDA remained uninitialized. All observed owned processes exited, no new SHM remained and the exclusive host lease was released. Full test output and all 27 evidence files were retained and hash-verified privately.

This qualifies the specified CPU diagnostic/prototype interfaces only. It establishes no native GPU-engine qualification, observation overhead, throughput improvement or real-query quality/latency benefit. Keep the PR Draft and unmerged.

Server GPU mechanism qualification completed on 2026-11-11 for exact head `b1d965fea7f84b19cb9f61974bdb263de8d854c3`.

The existing finite MMF program (Map → Map → Filter) used 16 source occurrences, two independent cold model instances and **48 real generate/add/final observations per arm, 96 total**, with no extra warmup or automatic retry. FIFO and `prefix_length` retained C4/B1, token budget 4096, Qwen2.5-7B, BF16, context 4096, native sequence cap 4, identical 8-token generation/seed 0/newline stop, full observer and Nsight settings. This is a project mechanism workload, not an original SemBench Q9 score.

- Both arms: 48 unique successful, submission-confirmed and terminal-confirmed calls; zero unknown calls. Each arm's full original-method replay passed all 48 saved responses with zero new model calls, and returned 7 final records.
- Call identities, complete prompt tokens, response text, parent links and finish reasons match 48/48. **Output token arrays match only 46/48.** At source positions 3 and 15 in the first Map, only the final token swaps between 271 (two newlines) and 151645 (`<|im_end|>`). The bound tokenizer confirms these decode differently; newline-stop/special-end removal explains the same returned text. The raw difference is retained: strict token equality did not pass, and this pair is not used for a performance advantage claim.
- Actual initial transport order changed from `[0,1,2,3]` to `[0,2,3,1]`; subsequent async frontiers also differ. Application transport batches were 15 versus 16. Native iteration-member samples were 116 versus 127. Both arms reported 2,080 cached and 1,646 computed prompt tokens. These are observed counts, not evidence of a cache or throughput improvement.

| Observed interval (seconds) | FIFO | prefix_length |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Controller cell wall | 94.037 | 97.256 |
| Worker wall | 74.716 | 78.063 |
| evaluate start → end | 43.526 | 44.911 |

These are one observation per arm. Worker wall includes startup, offline replay and collector shutdown; the evaluate interval includes the cold engine path. Neither interval is pure GPU time, and the trials do not establish stable speedup.

All four observer sinks per arm closed/flushed with zero recorded drops/errors; native generate/add/final counts are 48 each. Actual runner was `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner`; this head's added monolithic-v1 graph/cascade decisions were not observed and remain unknown. Raw Nsight reports are retained, but successful sink footers alone do not establish complete CUPTI/drop coverage; offline CUDA export is still pending. Telemetry missing fields remain missing.

Both models and all observed owned processes exited, GPU returned to idle, SHM was unchanged, and leases were released. The outer host helper separately removed four inactive, unreferenced private socket nodes per arm; this is external cleanup, not automatic author cleanup. Two earlier private-path/pre-worker failures were preserved and independently verified to have made zero model calls before this pair. All 283 listed evidence files were retrieved and individually hash-verified privately.

Functional response/relationship replay passed; strict token equality and a defensible performance comparison did not. No extra runs or tuning were added. Keep PR #98 Draft and unmerged.

Offline Nsight follow-up for exact head `b1d965fea7f84b19cb9f61974bdb263de8d854c3`, supplementing [the original GPU pair report](https://github.com/3444374/ai-operator-execution-optimization/pull/98#issuecomment-6784858383).

The earlier export had not started because an independent job held the shared host lease. Both original reports are now exported once to SQLite; integrity checks pass, both report hashes are unchanged, and all 283 original evidence files were reverified. This added **zero model calls or GPU collections**. The CPU export ran under the existing lease, CPU 0–7 and bounded supervisor; owned processes exited, SHM was unchanged and the lease was released.

| Observed records / calls | FIFO | Prefix-length |
|---|---:|---:|
| CUDA kernels | 42,714 | 46,194 |
| CUDA runtime API records | 22,404 | 23,708 |
| Successful `cudaGraphLaunch` API calls | 87 | 97 |
| Native sample markers matched to exported NVTX | 114/116 | 125/127 |

These are **whole-export counts**, not an evaluate/source-to-sink slice or equal-work performance comparison. The two unmatched sample markers in each arm are explicitly identified native initialization warmups. The actual EngineCore process has CUPTI/CUDA records and successful injection diagnostics. CUDA graph execution is observed, but it does not reconstruct the unobserved monolithic-v1 graph/cascade decision fields on the actual modular `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner` path.

Capture diagnostics warn that driver **13.2** was traced using **13.0** libraries, and retain partial NVTX/OSRT warnings for other processes. No explicit dropped-activity counter is available: absence of a loss diagnostic and zero drops in the four observer sinks **do not prove complete CUPTI/process-tree capture**. Produced-CUPTI and collected-CUDA counters have different scopes and their difference is not a measured drop count. Kernel-to-request attribution remains unproven; no activity-duration sum is presented as GPU wall time.

The prior result is unchanged: 48 requests per arm, matching returned text and final relation replay, but only **46/48 output token arrays** strictly equal. No speedup or stable performance advantage is claimed. Draft remains unmerged.
